article.story: HOUSTON -- — Mercy Miller had 23 points, Chendall Weaver added 14 points and No. 1 Houston beat Oakland 77-46 on Friday night in its first game since taking over the top spot in The AP Top 25 poll. Miller was 7 of 10 from the floor, including 3 of 6 from 3-point range, and Weaver was 6 of 8 from the field, including 2 of 3 from deep, as Houston (7-0) shot 50% from the field overall and 9 of 20 on 3-pointers. Houston outrebounded Oakland 39-20, had 21 assists on 27 made field goals, and turned 13 Oakland turnovers into 18 points. The Cougars moved to No. 1 after winning three games in three days in Las Vegas last week, including victories over then-No. 1 ranked Florida and No. 11 Kansas, en route to the Players Era 8 championship. Chris Fields Jr. had 10 points for Oakland (1-8). The Golden Grizzlies dropped to 0-8 on the road this season. Oakland shot 38% and was 7 of 22 on 3-pointers. The Cougars never trailed, jumping out to an 11-0 lead on two free throws by Delrecco Gillespie with 15:51 remaining in the first half. Houston’s lead grew to 21-2 on a 3-pointer by Weaver with 12:53 left in the half. The Cougars led 41-17 at halftime on 60% shooting. Up next Oakland: Hosts Northern Kentucky on Wednesday night. Houston: Hosts Queens on Sunday. ------ Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full men’s basketball coverage here
